newsitem.title: JAPAN: Possible NTT stock sale seen having limited impact.
newsitem.headline: Possible NTT stock sale seen having limited impact.

text.p: The possible sale of government-owned shares in Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) is unlikely to batter the overall stock market, brokers and analysts said on Thursday.
They said any impact from a possible sale would be limited to NTT's share price.

Business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said in its Thursday edition that the Ministry of Finance (MOF) planned to sell 500,000 NTT shares by the end of this year in the first such sale since fiscal 1988/89.
MOF said on Thursday it would not comment on whether it would sell NTT shares.

"It's hard to expect the market to be hurt by fresh sales of NTT shares because market sentiment has improved greatly recently on solid investor demand," said Hiroyuki Nakai, chief investment strategist at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.
MOF sold 5.4 million NTT shares in the three fiscal years up to March 1989, following the firm's privatisation in 1985, but it has put off further sales due to the Tokyo market's weakness.
Tokyo stocks have been supported by an influx of funds from public pension funds, which have aggressively sought shares in those blue-chip companies whose earnings prospects are bright, brokers said.
They said buying from cash-rich public institutions has encouraged other market participants to join the bandwagon, easing the downside risk for the market.

"We'll have to see how the market absorbs the NTT shares in the future, but I don't expect the (possible) sales alone to hit the overall market," said Kunihiro Hatae, general manager at Tokyo Securities Co Ltd.
On Thursday, NTT's shares lost 9,000 yen to 880,000. They had briefly dipped as low as 860,000.
The stock market's key barometer, the Nikkei 225 average, ended 37.40 points or 0.20 percent lower at 18,698.07.
